title: Multigrain Bread, Reduced Calorie, High Fiber, Toasted

content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain toasted bread with reduced calories and high fiber is a whole‑grain loaf made from a blend of several grains, seeds and bran, then toasted to a golden crust. It offers a crunchy texture and rich flavor while providing fewer calories and more dietary fiber than regular white bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Multigrain breads typically contain 5–8 different grains, such as oats, barley, rye and whole wheat.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a crisp crust while preserving most nutrients.
The high fiber content helps regulate blood sugar and supports digestive health.
Calorie reduction is achieved by using whole‑grain flours with lower energy density and adding leavening agents that create a lighter crumb.
Many multigrain breads are fortified with B‑vitamins and minerals like iron and magnesium.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion, promotes satiety and helps control blood glucose levels.

items.title: Reduced calorie content
items.content: Lower energy density makes the bread suitable for weight‑management diets without sacrificing taste.

items.title: Rich in micronutrients
items.content: The grain blend provides vitamin E, magnesium, zinc and iron, supporting metabolism and immunity.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs release energy slowly, maintaining stable energy throughout the day.

items.title: Heart‑healthy benefits
items.content: Fiber and healthy fats from seeds help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Grain allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic or intolerant to wheat, rye or other grains used in the loaf.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: The bread contains gluten and should be avoided by people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Certain varieties may contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread as a snack, in sandwiches, as toast, or alongside soups and salads. A toasted slice pairs well with avocado, low‑fat cottage cheese, turkey, or vegetable spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer‑safe bags and re‑toast before serving.
